tools.name: find_referencing_symbols
tools.title: Find referencing symbols
tools.description: Who calls this symbol, and what breaks if it changes? Fan-in for blast radius and error-path review: the symbols that reference a target, grouped by file and evidence tier. Each occurrence is tiered on its own binding: same-file, resolved-via-import, unique, or name-only-ambiguous, and a parameter or local of the same name is name-only. Read the top two tiers as callers and the bottom two as candidates; a group marked 'locals not checked' comes from a language with no scope analysis. 'unique' means only that the repository defines the name once, not that the two files are connected. Call it when the answer depends on who the callers are, not as a routine confirmation. It is the most expensive tool here, and fan-in across a large repository can take minutes.

target.description: Stable id, qualified name, or symbol name whose referencing symbols to find.

repo_root.description: Absolute path of the repository to read. Omit it when exactly one repository is selectable. A refusal lists the roots.

limit.description: Maximum reference sites listed, one per file in turn. Default 50.

shared_callers.description: Rank symbols whose callers overlap the target's, instead of listing references. This is the does-a-utility-already-exist check, and fuzzy retrieval evidence, not binding evidence.

tools.name: history
tools.title: History
tools.description: Why does this code exist? Return the commits that changed one symbol's lines at HEAD, newest first, with full message bodies. Failure is a refusal, never an empty answer. Call it to learn why, after another tool tells you where. It does not unlock the structural-first gate and is not loaded eagerly.

target.description: Stable id of the symbol, from a map, overview, find, explain or locate answer. A bare name is refused.

repo_root.description: Absolute path of the repository to read. Omit it when exactly one repository is selectable. A refusal lists the roots.

budget.description: Maximum approximate tokens spent on commit bodies. Default 12000.

tools.name: capabilities
tools.title: Capabilities
tools.description: Why is this answer incomplete? Report the server version, loaded grammars and their warm state, cache generation, the configured and client-advertised roots, and the caps in force. An absent tag cache is reported with the index command that builds it. Call it when a language seems unsupported, a generation mismatch persists, or the wrong root was selected.

repo_root.description: Absolute path of the repository to read. Omit it when exactly one repository is selectable. A refusal lists the roots.

tools.name: orient
tools.title: Orient
tools.description: Where does this code live, how is this repository shaped, how are two things connected? Start here. operation='map' (the structural entry point) takes focus, budget, limit and granularity: a token-budgeted skeleton of the highest-ranked files. It ranks and does not enumerate: limit defaults to 10 files, however large the repository. budget is counted with the server's chars/4 estimator: on this id-dense output a real BPE count runs 10-35% higher. Use grep for a known literal or file, and the map when the location is unknown or the change surface spans files. The map ranks symbols, so a file matched only by a string -- fixtures, config, resources -- does not appear. NOTE, WHY, HACK and TODO comments and ADR/RFC citations appear as rationale nodes below their symbol. operation='communities' (cheap) takes resolution and limit: which files belong together. Call it first in an unread repository, then map the group that matters. operation='cycles' (cheap) takes limit: every module-level import cycle. operation='diagram' takes focus, max_nodes, max_edges, group_by_communities and resolution: the module graph as a mermaid flowchart, for a human to read. operation='path' requires source and target and takes include_unique and include_ambiguous: the fewest-hop chain of resolved relationships between two endpoints. operation='health' takes limit: orphan candidates, unused exports and hubs, counted on same-file and resolved-via-import edges alone, plus erosion, clone share and complexity hotspots. Use it for dead code, architectural anchors and where complexity sits, not to find a bug. It does not judge design. Escalation chain: orient locates, symbols gives declarations and bodies, read gives exact lines.

operation.description: One of: map, communities, cycles, diagram, path, health. The tool description says what each one takes.

repo_root.description: Absolute path of the repository to read. Omit it when exactly one repository is selectable. A refusal lists the roots.

focus.description: File paths, path suffixes, module stems, or symbol names that seed the ranking. Paste a traceback frame, blob URL, absolute path or path:line as it appears: it seeds the file it names. A diagram uses the first entry alone.

budget.description: Maximum approximate tokens for the map. Omit it for automatic sizing in a 2000-8000 token band.

granularity.description: Map detail: function lists symbols in ranked files, file lists files alone, body adds budgeted bodies. Body replaces a map followed by an expand.

resolution.description: Modularity resolution. Larger values generally give smaller communities.

limit.description: Maximum rows for the selected operation: files, communities, cycles, or rows per health section, hotspots included. Health defaults to 20.

source.description: Path start: a stable id, qualified name, or file path.

target.description: Path end: a stable id, qualified name, or file path.

include_unique.description: Allow unique-name edges in a path. Off by default: a unique name is retrieval evidence, not binding evidence.

include_ambiguous.description: Allow name-only ambiguous edges in a path. Off by default: a spelling has several candidate definitions.

max_nodes.description: Maximum repository nodes drawn before an elision node is added.

max_edges.description: Maximum arrows drawn. The rest are counted in a comment.

group_by_communities.description: Group diagram nodes into deterministic community subgraphs.

no_cache.description: Parse every file live, bypassing the structural-fact cache.

tools.name: symbols
tools.title: Symbols
tools.description: You have a name, a file, or a stable id. Get its declaration, body, or wiring. operation='find' (cheap) requires name and takes kind and limit: symbols by substring or qualified name, each hit carrying file:line and a stable id. operation='overview' (cheap) requires paths and takes docstrings: the named files as signatures with bodies elided. Read it instead of the file. operation='expand' requires stable_ids and takes limit: the line-numbered body of each named symbol. Expand a long id alone, because an over-budget batch is shortened. operation='explain' requires target and takes limit: definition site, signature, rationale comments, fan-out and fan-in by evidence tier, and the file's imports. Start here with one suspect symbol. It replaces a find followed by a reference listing. operation='locate' (cheap) requires path and locations and takes context_lines: resolve class:, function: and line: strings to stable ids and merged intervals for one file. For who-calls-this and blast radius, use find_referencing_symbols. It is the expensive one.

operation.description: One of: find, overview, expand, explain, locate. The tool description says what each one requires.

repo_root.description: Absolute path of the repository to read. Omit it when exactly one repository is selectable. A refusal lists the roots.

name.description: Symbol name, qualified name, or substring to search for.

limit.description: Maximum rows for the selected operation. find and explain default to 20, expand to 10.

paths.description: Repository-relative source files to render as signatures with bodies elided.

docstrings.description: Include symbol docstrings in overviews. Default false.

stable_ids.description: Stable symbol identifiers printed by map, overview, find, explain and locate.

target.description: Stable id, qualified name, or symbol name. If several definitions tie, the first in path order is explained and the others are listed.

path.description: Repository-relative path of the source file, beneath the repository root.

locations.description: Location selectors: class:Name, function:name, or line:N.

context_lines.description: Lines added before and after each requested or resolved interval.

no_cache.description: Parse every file live, bypassing the structural-fact cache.

tools.name: read
tools.title: Read
tools.description: You need file contents rather than symbols: exact lines from one file, or the directory tree. operation='slice' requires path and takes lines, context_lines and whole_file: numbered lines for the requested ranges, with enclosing-scope headers. Prefer symbols operation 'expand' when a symbol boundary fits. operation='dir' (cheap) takes path, depth and max_entries: the repository's files as a gitignore-honouring tree.

operation.description: One of: slice, dir. The tool description says what each one takes.

repo_root.description: Absolute path of the repository to read. Omit it when exactly one repository is selectable. A refusal lists the roots.

path.description: Repository-relative path: the file for slice, the subtree for dir. dir defaults to the repository root.

lines.description: One or more 1-based inclusive [start, end] line ranges. Required unless whole_file is true.

context_lines.description: Lines added before and after each requested or resolved interval.

whole_file.description: Return the whole bounded file. Use it only when lines is omitted.

depth.description: Maximum directory levels below the tree root.

max_entries.description: Maximum entries rendered before the tree reports truncation.
